title: Teaching
text:
My approach to the classroom centers on creating a welcoming, low-stakes environment where students feel comfortable engaging with complex material. As an interdisciplinary scholar trained in criminology, sociology, geography, and public health, I aim to help students:

Connect Theory to Reality: Using guest speakers and current events to ground course concepts in the present.
Build Technical Skills: Leveraging 5+ years of experience in statistics and GIS to help students master data analysis.
Engage Meaningfully: Utilizing interactive tools like anonymous polling and live Q&A to reduce anxiety and increase participation.
Translate Knowledge: Designing assessments that emphasize the application of research to policy debates and real-world justice issues.

Status: In Progress (Supported by the College of Arts & Sciences Dissertation Research Fellowship)
This project investigates spatial disparities in harm reduction service availability (e.g., syringe service programs, naloxone distribution) across the United States. I examine how state-level policies interact with geographic context to create “service deserts,” with a specific focus on the unique structural barriers faced by rural communities.
Key Contribution: A replicable spatial framework for public health agencies and advocacy organizations to identify service gaps and evaluate policy impact.

title: Research
text:
Research Agenda
My research investigates the geography of harm, asking how structural conditions, such as state law, spatial inequality, and historical carceral practice, shape access to resources that support health and justice.
Working at the intersection of Criminology, Public Health, and Geography, I use a mixed-methods toolkit including: * Spatial Statistics & GIS (R, ArcGIS, ArcPro) * Qualitative Analysis (Interview transcription and data management) * Public-Facing Visualization (Interactive StoryMaps)

title: Research
text:
Digital Scholarship & Visualizations

Geographies of Isolation: Convict-Leased Black Women in the American South
As part of a collaborative project with Dr. Bonnie Ernst, I integrated archival sources with GIS to map the erased geographies of convict leasing. This work visualizes how punishment operated across a carceral landscape embedded in the post-Civil War South.






Featured Project: Interactive StoryMap



You can explore the spatial networks of this research through the interactive digital platform I developed: View the Geographies of Isolation StoryMap

title: Help Isn’t Everywhere: Mapping Access to Harm Reduction Services
text:
Status: In Progress · Supported by the College of Arts & Sciences Dissertation Research Fellowship
This dissertation investigates spatial disparities in harm reduction service availability across five U.S. states (California, Florida, Indiana, New York, and Ohio). I examine how state-level policies interact with geographic context to create “service deserts,” with particular attention to the structural barriers faced by rural communities.
Unit of analysis: County-level States: California, Florida, Indiana, New York, Ohio Service types: Syringe Service Programs (SSP), Naloxone Distribution, Supportive/Recovery Housing, Substance Use Treatment
